summary: SL-098 made tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 survive a TEMP it can create in but not list (the engine's C:\WINDOWS\TEMP). Every scratch removal now goes through a .NET-delete helper (Remove-ScratchDir) under one per-run root (Get-ScratchParent), B-008's root is padded to 250 characters (428 under both TEMPs), and SyncRootRig takes its parent from CloudRig.PrepareParent/TempTree. It shipped after one build attempt, with the acceptance test byte-identical and green. Validate ran RuleCases -Case All, WindowMutants -Mutant All and the opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT rig 3 times under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, all passing. The cost was in the gates: the design rested on a wrong investigation account of WindowCases.ps1, the critique halted once with 10 findings (5 major), and the code review ran twice.

payload.reason: Slice is complete. No candidates are raised: it was a follow-up two deep, so nothing it found lands on the backlog. The findings are in learned, unknowns and missed.
payload.estimate_error: Size (medium) and tier (medium) held: one build attempt, no loop, no product code (everything is under tests/ or eng-side scripts). The footprint was undercounted again, as lesson #388 predicts. The design named 11 components. The build's git diff 88e0824ca..76546c649 lists 10 modified files and 6 added files (the build commit reports 20 files), including two scripts the design did not plan to rewrite (SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1, SettledCountProbe.ps1) and five new test scripts plus a JSON corpus. Verification cost was higher than the code risk: RuleCases -Case All took 361 s and 363 s, WindowMutants 415 s, plus the full 805-test suite, the B-008 publish and the three opt-in cloud runs. Size such slices by the validation bill, not the diff. The brief also bundled five merged reports (SC-161, 160, 163, 164, 171) and had only a title, so the design had to assume what "RuleCases.ps1 is not touched" meant.

learned.lesson: A merged-in complaint's line-number claims must be re-read in the file at design time, not copied from the investigation. The design built Get-CloudRigParent, a contract, a case, a TempRoots check and a WindowCases fitness rule on the investigation's statement that WindowCases.ps1:5680/:5747 list GetTempPath() for 'fsa-cf-*'. Those lines are Get-CloudCaseBase and Clear-StaleCloudRoots, which already apply the Windows-folder rule and list N-006's own fsa-window-cloud roots. The engine had also already appended the matching fitness entry, so the builder had to delete it by hand. Check engine-appended fitness entries against the final design before building.
learned.evidence: Critique M1 (decided accepted-pending); O-016 'not mutable ... absence'; build removed the engine-appended WindowCases rule from .taad/fitness.yaml (was :1170-1177) and wrote no Get-CloudRigParent.

learned.lesson: Any helper added to tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 must run under Windows PowerShell 5.1 as well as pwsh 7. SettledCountProbe.ps1 and SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 run copies of RuleCases under powershell.exe and pwsh. The design imported TempTree.cs idioms (IsPathFullyQualified, LinkTarget, EnumerationOptions) that are .NET Core-only. The build used a drive/UNC regex and Attributes instead. Anything written in RuleCases needs the powershell.exe repeat, and the Get-ScratchParent branch that the engine's TEMP takes (the Windows-folder branch) is the one that would have broken.
learned.evidence: Critique M3; O-018; SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 repeats all checks under powershell.exe 5.1 and kills the IsPathFullyQualified mutant (5.1); code review ran -Case C-003 and C-004 whole under 5.1 with TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.

learned.lesson: Every .ps1 under tests/ that roots scratch in GetTempPath() or calls Remove-Item is red under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, and an unfixed run leaves folders only an administrator can list. This slice fixed RuleCases, SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1. The last two were already failing there at HEAD, which the design had not known. Still unfixed: SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 (New-TempDir and the finally near :641), SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1, WindowMutants.ps1, PoolWatchCases.ps1 and the other tests/bugs/*.ps1. Before running any of them under the engine's TEMP, grep it for GetTempPath/Remove-Item or point TEMP at a listable folder first. The build's pre-fix runs added fsa-settled-probe-* and two fsa-sl076-* folders to the Q-219 admin-cleanup pile (the two fsa-sl076-* were removed by exact name).
learned.evidence: Build deviation notes: HEAD SL-076 failed under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (ShortName finds no 8.3 name, its own cleanup denied); SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells exited 1 and left fsa-settled-probe-*. Lesson #372 predicted the class.

learned.lesson: Never express a TEMP-dependent check as `pwsh -Command "$env:TEMP=...; pwsh -File ..."`. The outer PowerShell expands the variables inside the double quotes, the assignment fails as a non-terminating error, and the inner run uses whatever TEMP it inherited, so it can pass under the wrong one. The loop's test_command also cannot carry shell syntax. Use a wrapper script that sets TEMP/TMP in the process environment and runs -File, and have the script under test print the TEMP it saw ('scratch: <root> (TEMP <GetTempPath()>)') so the check can assert it. SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 and SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1 are that pattern.
learned.evidence: Critique M4; build deviation on wrapper scripts; validate's -Temp Engine and -Temp Ordinary runs both asserted the scratch line's TEMP.

learned.lesson: In RuleCases.ps1, Check writes with Write-Output, so any function that returns a value (New-TempDir, Invoke-HarnessRaw) turns into an array when something it calls prints. SL-098-ReturnValues.Tests.ps1 plus SL-098-ReturnValueCorpus.json is a closed census of every function in RuleCases.ps1. A new function without a row fails it. The next slice that adds a function to RuleCases.ps1 must add its row, and should print through Write-Host, Out-Host or Out-Null.
learned.evidence: Critique m2 / O-022; corpus has 27 fire/quiet plants and 9 dynamic rows. The pre-fix variants fail D01, D08, D09 and the census check.

learned.lesson: Remove-ScratchDir does not remove a junction that is itself marked ReadOnly. It leaves the junction, counts one 'cleanup:' FAIL and does not throw, and nothing crosses the link. Through Remove-ScratchDir the hand walk never sees a junction, because the first Directory.Delete unlinks plain ones before it stops on a read-only file (dotnet/runtime#86249). The walk's reparse rule is only exercised by extracting the nested Open-Tree and feeding it directly. Any new test of the helper's link handling must use that route and include a +R reparse point.
learned.evidence: Validate O-014 probe, entry j2ro (attrib +r /L): [failed]. Build deviation m1. Code review round 2 table has six shapes and no read-only junction.

learned.lesson: A human answer that grants validate a run (Q-086: Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT three times in a row) must become an open obligation owed to validate-slice when the critique decision is made. Here the build marked O-020 discharged by a default-suite Fact and sent the real run to a person, which contradicted Q-086 and M5. Code review caught it, the engine waived it (O-026), and validate ran the three runs anyway because Q-086 allowed it. They passed 3/3 (4 Facts each, no fsa-cf-* folder, no CfProvider, sync-root count unchanged). The outcome was right by luck. Do not rely on the waive path to carry a person's standing permission.
learned.evidence: Code review m1 / O-026 waived to SC-226; validate: 'settles Derived 7 and the run that was waived as O-026'; build 'LEFT OPEN: PERSON: run the opt-in rig once'.

learned.lesson: Budget about 30 minutes of validation for any slice that changes RuleCases.ps1 or WindowCases.ps1. RuleCases -Case All needs the engine python (%APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe, -EngineRoot taad_v3\backend) and runs ~361 s per TEMP. Q-114 makes WindowMutants -Mutant All required for WindowCases edits (415 s), and the B-008 publish runs on top. The build-check missed the venv python because it searched only inside taad_v3, so Derived 3 was 'unknown' until the spikes' path was reused. Hand the venv path to the build-check for any RuleCases slice.
learned.evidence: Validate: 361 s (Engine TEMP), 363 s (Ordinary), WindowMutants 415 s; build-check commands 7-9 found no python.exe and C:\Python314 failed `import yaml`; design 'Gaps in earlier stages'.

learned.lesson: RuleCases -Case All runs get killed mid-way by something that does not wait the ~360 s they need, and each kill leaves a fsa-rulecases-<hex> root of about 140 folders (134-ish fsa-parity-case-* plus 6 fsa-engine-case-*) in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. The per-run root makes them findable, but nothing deletes them. Validate found four such roots started at exact 2-minute intervals (looks like a 120 s timeout), and code review found two more made by the engine's own post-build proving runs. Run -Case All in the background or with a longer timeout, and do not count these leftovers against the slice that finds them.
learned.evidence: Validate 'Leftovers seen': four fsa-rulecases-* roots with 140-141 folders each; code review 'Leftovers': fsa-rulecases-0879ca0938 and fsa-rulecases-3bd86f4f0e, 134 parity + 6 engine each, created 2 minutes apart after the build commit. Q-132, lesson #274.

lessons_judged.why: It predicted the class exactly: scripts outside Core.Tests inherit C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and Remove-Item is denied. The slice chose its own root and [IO.Directory]::Delete, and found SL-076 and SettledCountProbe red there at HEAD.
B-008 got a fixed 250-character root (428 under both TEMPs) instead of repointing TEMP, as the lesson advised.
N-006 and Complete-CloudSeamRun were left unchanged. The only contact was critique M1, which found by reading code that Get-CloudCaseBase already roots in LocalAppData\Temp.
Deletion was routed through [IO.Directory]::Delete. The engine's guard also blocked a Remove-Item probe on a system path in the build-check, as the lesson warned.
Every check ran under both TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. That is how SL-076 and SettledCountProbe were found already red under the engine's TEMP.

The per-run root was placed in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp so killed-run leftovers are findable, and the printed 'scratch:' path let validate check by name. Note that since TempTree routes away from C:\Windows\Temp, nothing roots in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests any more.

It predicted the footprint undercount: 11 designed components against a build diff of 10 modified and 6 added files. The design's instruction to grep for pins of the fitness except_files list came from it.
The design flagged that C-001/C-003 recount settled entries after the appended fitness rule, and -Case All (C-001..C-014) went green under both TEMPs.
The venv python and -EngineRoot command from the lesson drove harness.py --scenario all (117 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits) and the RuleCases -Case All runs.
The long runs (~6 min each, WindowMutants ~7 min) were budgeted and run last. The leftover roots show something still kills -Case All at about 120 s, shorter than the 600 s limit the lesson assumes.
The WindowCases.ps1 B-008 edit stayed ASCII and CRLF. Code review checked that every changed .ps1 is ASCII.
B-008 was verified through the publish recipe plus WindowCases -Case B-008 (SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1), because dotnet test never runs the window cases.
Everything ran through eng/dotnet.ps1. The build-check still triggered a 300 MB SDK 10.0.401 download into the worktree's .dotnet, as the lesson says each fresh worktree does.
All builds, tests and publishes went through eng/dotnet.ps1, and validate checked that fsa-tests held no fsa-cf-* folder afterwards.
The Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT runs were treated as measurements. The critique decision worded failures as 'recorded, not blamed on the routing'. All three runs passed, so the clause was never exercised.

missed.what: The critique (M2, M3) put SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1 into the cases to be run under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. It never asked whether those scripts root scratch in GetTempPath() or use Remove-Item themselves, which lesson #372 had handed over. Both already failed under that TEMP at HEAD (SL-076: ShortName and its own denied cleanup; SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells: exit 1). The build had to rewrite both beyond the design, and its first runs of the unfixed scripts left fsa-settled-probe-* and two fsa-sl076-* folders in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. A check would be: for every script a case adds to the TEMP matrix, grep it for GetTempPath, $env:TEMP and Remove-Item before listing it as a consumer.
missed.caught_by: build (deviation notes; HEAD copy measured under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP)

missed.what: The design marked 'RuleCases killed before its finally runs' as non-material (no test), and the critique did not challenge it. Q-132 already said killed runs are the main source of leaked scratch. In practice -Case All (~360 s) is killed at about 120 s by whatever drives it. Validate found four fsa-rulecases-* roots of 140-141 folders each, started exactly 2 minutes apart, and had to kill a C-004 run by hand to prove the leftovers are findable. A check would be: the critique should ask what the leftover looks like and who removes it, and require a kill-mid-run case when the loop's own timeouts are known to be shorter than the run.

Remove-ScratchDir leaves behind a junction that is itself marked ReadOnly. It records one 'cleanup:' FAIL and throws nothing; the outside files stay untouched. Code review round 2 tried six shapes (read-only subfolder, read-only top folder, Hidden+System+ReadOnly file, nested read-only folders, trailing separator, file at path) and declared 'found nothing new', but fed no read-only reparse point. The critique's m1 fix asked for unlinking each reparse point and likewise did not ask about +R on the link. Validate's independent O-014 probe (entry j2ro, attrib +r /L) found it.

unknowns: Does the engine's own stage-shell token behave like this user's interactive session? Every run here set TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP inside the interactive session. SC-215 (Remove-Item denied under the engine token) and SC-216 (a possible TMPDIR in the stage shell) were not reproduced. Whether [IO.Directory]::Delete of the harness's fsa-rules-* scratch in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP works under the engine token is unmeasured.

Do the SL-069 sibling tests (tests/bugs/SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1, SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1) still hold after this slice's RuleCases changes (scratch line, per-run root, Remove-ScratchDir, two more settled-rule markers)? No stage ran them (513-630 s each). Code review only noted that the SettledMarkers shape in EveryCaseFollowsCounts was already red at HEAD 88e0824, because the last settled marker there was SL-096, not SL-069. SL-098 appended another marker, so that red persists.
What drives RuleCases -Case All and kills it at about 120 s? Four fsa-rulecases-* roots started at 2-minute intervals suggest a 120 s timeout, but who ran them and with what limit was not observed.

Did validate's Engine-TEMP -Case All leave any harness fsa-rules-* folder directly in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP? This user cannot list it. The only evidence is that the helper printed no 'cleanup:' line. Older leftovers there (SC-214, Q-219, fsa-settled-probe-*) still need an elevated listing.
Windows 10 was never run (no machine, Q-205/Q-216). Get-ScratchParent, the ACL behaviour of %SystemRoot%\Temp and the cldflt rig are measured on Windows 11 build 26200 only.
what_went_wrong: The design built a whole component set (Get-CloudRigParent, its contract, case, TempRoots check, and the WindowCases fitness rule) on the investigation's wrong account of WindowCases.ps1:5680/:5747. The design stage did not read those lines, and its own hedge ('if they turn out not to look for SyncRootRig's roots, they are left alone') contradicted its contracts. The engine had already appended the matching fitness rule, so the build had to delete an engine-written entry by hand.

The critique halted once with 10 findings, 5 of them major (M1 wrong WindowCases account; M2 SL-076 broken unnamed; M3 5.1 compatibility; M4 TEMP assignment in a quoted -Command; M5 opt-in rig unexecuted). All were real. The design's brief was only a title and five merged complaints, and the design leaned on the investigation rather than the files.

The build-check could not find the engine's venv python because it searched only inside taad_v3, so Derived 3 (-Case All with a listable TEMP) stayed 'unknown' until the design pointed at %APPDATA%\taad3\venv. It also triggered the 300 MB SDK download again.

The build ran the unfixed SettledCountProbe and SL-076 under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and left fsa-settled-probe-* and fsa-sl076-* folders there. The fsa-sl076-* ones were removed by exact name; the fsa-settled-probe-* ones need an administrator, adding to the Q-219 pile.

The build declared O-020 discharged while sending the real Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT run to a person, which contradicted Q-086 and M5. Code review caught it and the engine waived it (O-026). Validate ran the three runs anyway, so the waiver text 'nothing else is sending this stage back' was wrong.

Code review ran twice. The first round halted on 4 'undeclared departures' that were all declared or decided, and one entry literally reads 'No undeclared departure was found', so the halt cost a lap. Its two real minors were waived to the backlog: SC-225 (the wrapper's default -EngineRoot only resolves from a slice worktree, so the documented commands in SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 fail from the main checkout) and SC-226.

Shipped with known loose ends: stale %TEMP% comments (CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:19 and :251, CloudRig.cs:10 and :22, SC-224), no repo test showing the new RuleCases Remove-Item fitness rule can fire (SC-223; code review checked it by hand only), and a read-only junction that Remove-ScratchDir leaves behind with a counted FAIL.

The bug report had only a title, so two readings had to be assumed. One was that 'RuleCases.ps1 is not touched by this slice' was SL-091's filing note, not a limit on SL-098; it is unconfirmed by a person.
